status: first proposal; job families reasonable working basis; responsibilities and homes provisional

features.title: Record scope, evidence homes, and decision responsibilities
features.minimum: A recorded agreement names product scope, record types, authoritative homes, link meanings, responsible people, and applicable checks.
features.later: Configurable scope/role profiles and rules selected for each engagement.
features.external: Responsible BBT/client owners must agree the first scope and permitted decision roles.
features.example: A requirement has one agreed home and named author/reviewer; the team can identify who resolves an ownership conflict.
features.reuse: Product rules and an authority explanation are documented; engagement-level configuration is a broader proposal.

features.title: Identify and retain exact record versions
features.minimum: Use stable IDs, exact revisions, source references, and distinct candidate/accepted states in the selected record home. A small agreed record set is enough to start.
features.later: Internal editing/history for more evidence types, with cross-system identity mappings and concurrency handling.
features.external: The chosen home must support, or be supplemented with, usable version references and accessible history.
features.example: A reviewer can open the source and requirement revisions used by a check even after the latest versions change.
features.reuse: Evidence versions, source revisions, and retained baselines are described in the demo data model.

features.title: Define trace meanings and allowed relationships
features.minimum: Define a small vocabulary with endpoint types, direction, meaning, and review expectations for the first workflow.
features.later: Versioned policies covering additional evidence types and conditional coverage rules.
features.external: Domain owners must agree what a link establishes and which links are expected for the selected scope.
features.example: A need-to-requirement link means derivation, while a requirement-to-test link names verification scope; neither transfers approval.
features.reuse: A controlled prototype relationship policy is documented; the wider map vocabulary still needs agreement.

features.title: Record human decisions and return work for revision
features.minimum: Retain the named person, role, object/version, reason, and accept/revise/reject/defer outcome. An existing review process can supply the decision.
features.later: Integrated review queues, reminders, permission enforcement, and authenticated decision capture for the selected deployment.
features.external: A designated reviewer and an agreed decision record are required; a checker finding remains separate from approval.
features.example: Editing a submitted requirement prevents an earlier acceptance from applying to the new wording.
features.reuse: Revision-bound prototype decisions and return-to-author history are documented; simulated personas do not establish production identity.

features.title: Version processing instructions and retain run provenance
features.minimum: Select an agreed prompt, output schema, source/context revisions, and model configuration; retain result, validation failures, and run identity.
features.later: A managed policy registry, richer run comparison, and evaluated configuration changes.
features.external: A method owner agrees the initial instructions, output contract, and evaluation examples.
features.example: Two drafts can be compared using their exact inputs and prompt versions; a failed output does not become accepted evidence.
features.reuse: Versioned source/context/needs/requirements/impact contracts and run records are documented.

features.title: Capture source material manually with citations
features.minimum: Paste or upload supported text; retain origin, revision, captured content, and exact locators. Record duplicate capture without duplicating the interpretation work.
features.later: Additional source formats and assisted selection of relevant spans.
features.external: A usable source and the selected capture destination must be available.
features.example: A pasted transcript remains identifiable, and a draft need points to the exact quoted passage.
features.reuse: Text/Markdown source intake and source-derived provenance are documented.

features.title: Extract source text from documents
features.minimum: Extract supported text-based PDF/DOCX content with page/paragraph locators, original file references, and visible extraction warnings.
features.later: Additional formats and separately evaluated OCR where needed.
features.external: Representative files, extraction limits, and a decision about retaining the original bytes are required.
features.example: A requirement citation opens the correct paragraph in the imported document revision.
features.reuse: WP-30 document intake and anchored extraction are recorded as local work in the delivery plan; acceptance status is not rechecked here.

features.title: Capture selected Slack discussions
features.minimum: Import a selected thread with message IDs, author/time, edits, and source references into the common intake path.
features.later: Scoped ongoing observation, edited/deleted-message handling, and recoverable capture.
features.external: The selected workspace, access permissions, capture scope, and retention expectations must be agreed.
features.example: A thread becomes a cited source without implying that every message is an approved product decision.
features.reuse: No live Slack connector is established by the current documentation.

features.title: Capture meeting transcripts and associated notes
features.minimum: Import an identified transcript/notes pair with meeting date, speaker/time locators where supplied, and revision references.
features.later: A selected meeting-platform connection and recovery of later transcript corrections.
features.external: The selected transcript source, access, and interpretation of speaker/time metadata must be agreed.
features.example: A candidate decision cites a transcript passage while a later correction creates a new source revision.
features.reuse: Manual source intake offers a reuse path; a live meeting-platform connector is not established.

features.title: Ask and resolve clarification questions
features.minimum: Identify ambiguous or unsupported statements, assign questions, and retain answers/deferrals with their source and rationale.
features.later: Assisted question generation, discipline routing, and richer conflict handling.
features.external: Someone with the relevant product/domain knowledge must be available to answer material questions.
features.example: An unclear alert threshold produces a question rather than an invented numeric requirement.
features.reuse: Source-context questions with required/advisory handling are documented.

features.title: Draft needs and requirements from agreed evidence
features.minimum: Run an agreed prompt to produce a small structured batch of cited candidate needs/requirements and proposed links. Required clarifications and relevant risk/task inputs enter the context. Derived requirements use reviewed needs; parent acceptance does not approve the resulting requirement.
features.later: Additional evidence types, tailored schemas, and improved drafting based on evaluated feedback.
features.external: Agree the output type, destination, source context, and representative evaluation examples. Risk/task inputs may be supplied externally.
features.example: A transcript creates a candidate need and measurable requirement with citations; the reviewer corrects unsupported detail before acceptance.
features.reuse: Needs/requirements drafting is documented; the full risk/usability-before-requirements workflow remains broader than the existing source-first slice.

features.title: Check and revise the worker's draft
features.minimum: Apply defined checks for schema, measurability, units, citations, and link rules. Record findings; a person or drafting agent revises and rechecks within a bounded loop.
features.later: Targeted agent repairs, additional domain rules, and tool-assisted checking.
features.external: Agree the check criteria and retry/escalation limits for each output type.
features.example: A requirement missing a measurable criterion is revised or routed to a person; exhausting retries leaves the issue visible.
features.reuse: Schema/provenance validation and deterministic checks are documented; a general autonomous revise/recheck loop is a proposed increment.

features.title: Find and assemble relevant existing evidence
features.minimum: Open a curated set of referenced records and exact versions from their homes; retain the context selection and mark unavailable evidence.
features.later: Search, filtering, semantic retrieval, and independently selected context bundles.
features.external: Read access and usable references to the evidence needed by the selected job.
features.example: A requirement reviewer can inspect the existing need, risk control, and related test without relying on the drafting agent's summary.
features.reuse: Evidence browsing, graph neighborhoods, and bounded impact retrieval are documented.

features.title: Propose and review trace-link changes
features.minimum: Create, confirm, retype, or retire a link with defined meaning, endpoint/version context, rationale, and a separate decision.
features.later: Bulk proposal review and changes launched from the graph, matrix, or change work.
features.external: The authoritative link home and reviewer must be agreed. Existing external link controls can supply this capability.
features.example: Rejecting a suggested test link leaves the suggestion in history and keeps it out of the confirmed trace set.
features.reuse: WP-10 controlled relationship lifecycle is documented as accepted at prototype scope.

features.title: Inspect traceability and identify defined coverage gaps
features.minimum: Show a read-only matrix/neighborhood from identifiable accepted links and report missing relationships under named scope rules.
features.later: Candidate-state comparison, richer domain coverage, and explainable gap priorities.
features.external: A usable relationship set and agreed coverage expectations. The set may be imported from a bought tool.
features.example: A control lacking an applicable verification test is visible with the reason and affected version.
features.reuse: Matrix, graph, coverage rules, and candidate projections are documented.

features.title: Coordinate a change and its follow-up work
features.minimum: Record old/proposed states, reason, scope, impact decisions, owners, and update/relink/retest tasks; retain unresolved work.
features.later: Integrated review queues, task synchronization, and workflow rules for different change classes.
features.external: Agree what constitutes a significant change, the responsible disciplines, and the chosen work home.
features.example: A threshold change has named requirement, risk, test, and label follow-up with separate dispositions.
features.reuse: Controlled change, impact decisions, return-to-author, and reanalysis are documented.

features.title: Trace the known consequences of a change
features.minimum: Traverse known links under defined bounds and show why each record is in the review set.
features.later: Configurable traversal and collection/configuration-aware impact context.
features.external: Relevant links and a declared traversal policy must be available; an empty graph cannot establish absence of impact.
features.example: The reviewer can follow the path from the changed requirement to a control and verification plan.
features.reuse: Bounded graph/collection candidate selection and path origins are documented.

features.title: Independently check a candidate or change
features.minimum: Use a separate reviewer or checker with underlying sources, explicit criteria, and independently selected context. Record findings, coverage limits, and exact examined versions.
features.later: Automated broader checks using separately configured model/prompt/context choices, with evaluated independence and miss/false-alarm measures.
features.external: An independent checker and relevant evidence access are needed. Formal approval remains a separate decision.
features.example: The outer check catches an affected control or test omitted by the worker and sends a finding to the responsible person.
features.reuse: Impact assistance and deterministic coherence checks offer components; the documented workflow does not establish a fully independent outer-check design.

conditional.when: Checking a significant change with assigned follow-up

features.title: Suggest missing relationships and unlinked impacts
features.minimum: Search supplied records beyond known links and propose cited possible relationships/impacts; people confirm or reject them.
features.later: Improved retrieval and evaluations that measure consequential misses and unhelpful suggestions.
features.external: A representative evidence corpus, review criteria, and access to records outside the current linked neighborhood.
features.example: A relevant label outside the confirmed graph appears as a possible impact and stays provisional until reviewed.
features.reuse: Semantic impact candidates are documented; similarity remains distinct from controlled traceability.

features.title: Detect source and implementation drift
features.minimum: Compare captured old/new observations, distinguish duplicates from material changes, and route meaningful drift to review without rewriting accepted records.
features.later: Continuous scoped observation and recoverable synchronization.
features.external: The previous observed revision and current source access must be available.
features.example: A changed transcript or commit creates review work while the prior requirement and baseline retain their original basis.
features.reuse: Source-revision drift is documented; live work-system observations are broader planned work.

features.title: Connect design, work, code, and builds
features.minimum: Author or reference design records and manually associate requirement/component IDs, tasks, commits, PRs, and builds with reviewed link meanings.
features.later: Assisted as-built comparison and synchronized implementation references.
features.external: Access to the selected work/repository/build systems and agreement on design granularity.
features.example: A reviewer can identify the design rationale, work item, and exact implementation revision associated with a requirement.
features.reuse: Component evidence exists in the product model; live repository/work-tracker connections remain planned in the documentation.

features.title: Observe work-tracker records
features.minimum: Capture a selected ticket revision, assignment/state, and controlled-record references using a defined mapping.
features.later: Event-driven capture and deliberate exchange of follow-up tasks without duplicating product truth.
features.external: Select the tracker, access, field mapping, and task-state authority.
features.example: A ticket update becomes an observation; moving a ticket to Done does not accept a requirement.
features.reuse: Fixture-backed work observations are planned in WP-40; no live connector is established here.

features.title: Observe repository and PR revisions
features.minimum: Capture exact commits, paths, PR decisions, and build references with origin and mapping metadata.
features.later: Scoped event handling and assisted comparison between intended and observed implementation.
features.external: Select repository/PR access and the observation scope; code presence does not establish product intent.
features.example: A changed threshold is associated with its commit and relevant evidence without silently changing a requirement.
features.reuse: Repository observation is described as planned product direction.

features.title: Capture CI executions and report evidence
features.minimum: Import a run/report bundle with exact build/test references, provenance, result checks, and file integrity; retain the execution and its review separately.
features.later: A selected live CI connection with authenticated run observations and recoverable report capture.
features.external: Agree CI report formats, required checks, test/build mappings, and read access.
features.example: A green pipeline from a different commit cannot provide current evidence for the proposed build.
features.reuse: Manual verified GitHub Actions bundle import is documented; a live CI connector is not established.

features.title: Run checks in normal PR and work-item workflows
features.minimum: Provide an explicit command/action from the chosen developer workflow that checks named revisions and reports findings there with evidence links.
features.later: Event-triggered checks and agreed tool-native gates for defined significant changes.
features.external: Select the event/command surface, criteria, write permissions for results, and ownership of any gate.
features.example: A PR author sees independent requirement/risk/test findings before the significant change proceeds.
features.reuse: Thin developer-tool controls are identified as a gap in the charter alignment notes.

features.title: Manage verification plans, executions, and dispositions
features.minimum: Maintain a test plan at a named V-model level, link its criterion to the checked item, record an exact execution/configuration, and review the outcome.
features.later: More execution formats, regression selection, suite-level coverage, and stale-evidence detection.
features.external: Test owners, criteria, build/environment identity, and access to original execution evidence.
features.example: A failed execution creates an anomaly; a rerun is a new execution and does not erase the failure.
features.reuse: WP-20A test-plan/execution/review controls are documented at fictional prototype scope.

features.title: Support risk analysis, controls, and residual-risk review
features.minimum: Maintain or reference risk records and controls, their requirement/test links, supporting evidence, and named risk decisions.
features.later: Domain-specific analysis forms, control effectiveness checks, and broader risk-change assistance.
features.external: Risk owners, criteria, relevant analyses, and supporting evidence appropriate to the selected product scope.
features.example: Changing a control exposes the requirement/test evidence and residual-risk decision that need review.
features.reuse: Hazard/control evidence and WP-20B residual-risk decisions are documented; a complete risk authoring system is broader work.

features.title: Support tasks, UI requirements, and usability evidence
features.minimum: Maintain or reference user tasks, critical tasks, UI requirements, study versions, and resulting review actions.
features.later: Dedicated formative/summative workflow and assisted use-related coverage checks.
features.external: Usability owner, task identities, study evidence, and applicability to the selected scope.
features.example: A critical task can be followed through the UI requirement to its evaluation outcome.
features.reuse: General clinical/usability evidence is in the product model; a dedicated usability workflow is not established.

features.title: Support validation and claim-evidence review
features.minimum: Maintain or reference protocols/results per need or claim, their evaluation configuration, limitations, and review decisions.
features.later: Dedicated study/evidence-package workflows and domain-specific coverage checks.
features.external: Validation/domain owners, criteria, population/scenario scope, and original evaluation evidence.
features.example: A claim unsupported by the selected study remains an unresolved finding even if system tests pass.
features.reuse: Clinical evidence and validation links appear in the product model; a full validation workflow is not established.

features.title: Author and review labelling and instructions
features.minimum: Maintain controlled label content with source requirements, supported claims, limitations, risk disclosures, and separate review.
features.later: Template-assisted label authoring, cross-version comparison, and broader consistency checks.
features.external: Label owner and applicable claim/risk evidence; the authoritative content home remains provisional.
features.example: Changing a performance claim identifies the label wording and supporting evidence that must be reconsidered.
features.reuse: Label evidence/change scenarios are documented; dedicated label authoring remains broader work.

features.title: Associate model and dataset versions with product evidence
features.minimum: Reference dataset/model identities, provenance, partitions, training configuration, locked-test criteria, and the exact build/evaluation using them.
features.later: Adapters to selected registries and domain-specific split/performance/change checks.
features.external: An applicable ML scope, accessible artifact versions, and agreed data/model ownership and criteria.
features.example: A performance report tied to model A does not establish performance of a release containing model B.
features.reuse: Dataset/model records are in the wider planning map, with no dedicated implemented workflow established here.

features.title: Review and freeze an exact evidence baseline
features.minimum: Select exact evidence/link versions, inspect current decisions and coherence, and record a separate baseline decision while retaining the prior state.
features.later: Richer baseline comparison and checks for more evidence families.
features.external: A baseline authority and the evidence scope/decision criteria must be agreed. A bought-tool baseline can supply the capability.
features.example: A later requirement edit creates new candidate work while documents from the previous baseline remain reproducible.
features.reuse: Immutable baseline selection, projections, decisions, and retained history are documented.

features.title: Render and review baseline-linked document packages
features.minimum: Use an agreed template to assemble a version-identifiable document/package from exact baseline membership, then review completeness.
features.later: Governed template versions, automated PDF/DOCX/ZIP outputs, and meaningful redlines.
features.external: Document owners, required outputs, templates, and access to baseline evidence.
features.example: A specification identifies the evidence versions it contains and explains differences from the prior output.
features.reuse: WP-30 controlled snapshots/templates/packages are recorded as local work; this exercise does not revalidate acceptance.

features.title: Assemble release evidence and a separate decision
features.minimum: Join the named baseline/build to applicable current support, open-issue dispositions, and required distinct release/transfer decisions.
features.later: Automated freshness/readiness checks and richer transfer packages for the selected scope.
features.external: Agree release scope, required evidence, decision authorities, and the selected release home.
features.example: A changed test, label, or risk decision makes the relevant readiness assessment subject to recheck.
features.reuse: WP-20B final-release controls are documented at fictional prototype scope, with specified support and role limits.

conditional.when: Risk acceptance is required for this release
Model/data versions are part of the release

features.title: Capture corrections and failure feedback
features.minimum: Retain before/after, reason, relevant record/source/method versions, and subsequent outcome when someone corrects or rejects work.
features.later: Structured failure categories and feedback capture embedded in every review surface.
features.external: Agree a small feedback record and responsibility for completing it. Start with human edits and rejections.
features.example: A reviewer changing an invented threshold records what changed and why, rather than leaving only the final wording.
features.reuse: Audit and correction histories offer source material; a joined meta-loop feedback workflow is not established.

features.title: Review recurring corrections and failures
features.minimum: A process owner periodically groups feedback, investigates causes, and records proposed improvements; a spreadsheet or simple query can suffice.
features.later: Assisted pattern summaries across suitable projects, with access-aware aggregation and follow-up tracking.
features.external: A named process owner, review cadence, sufficient context, and appropriate access to project feedback.
features.example: Repeated missing control links lead to an investigation of context selection rather than repeated one-off instructions.
features.reuse: The loop concept comes from the user's framing; a recurring cross-project review workflow is proposed.

features.title: Evaluate and adopt improved working methods
features.minimum: Propose a versioned prompt/rule/context/tool change, evaluate failure examples and previously correct cases, record adoption, and observe later regressions.
features.later: A richer evaluation library, comparisons by method version, and monitored rollout.
features.external: A method owner, representative reviewed examples, evaluation criteria, and an adoption decision.
features.example: A new context rule catches the missed label while preserving correct previous decisions; it changes future methods without rewriting product records.
features.reuse: Prompt evaluation and offline regression precedents are documented; continuous meta-loop adoption is broader work.

features.title: Exchange records and preserve a handover path
features.minimum: Define a small import/export contract for the first workflow, preserve IDs/provenance/decisions, and record the accepted target IDs. Manual transfer can suffice.
features.later: Selected API adapters, broader history/attachment exchange, and rehearsed migration of scoped record ownership.
features.external: Agree the destination's supported format and ownership boundary; confirm access to history and relationships before a handover.
features.example: Accepted drafts reach the chosen evidence home with their source references and decisions; the team can retrieve them there without a second authoritative copy.
features.reuse: Document packages and an authority model offer pieces; supplier-neutral exchange and handover are proposed.

features.title: Run background work with visible status and recovery
features.minimum: Give unattended capture/check operations durable identities, explicit queued/running/failed/completed states, bounded retries, duplicate handling, and a recovery path.
features.later: Broader job coordination, concurrency protection, cost limits, and operational monitoring.
features.external: Agree operating environment, ownership of failed work, and recovery/retention expectations.
features.example: A connector retry captures the same source revision once; a failed check remains visible and cannot be mistaken for a passing review.
features.reuse: Run failures are documented; durable jobs/recovery and related production foundations are deferred in the delivery plan.

packages.title: Agree conventions and a usable exchange path
packages.outcome: The first workflow has agreed record identities, homes, review responsibilities, processing contracts, and a way to transfer accepted outputs.
packages.gate: One sample source, candidate, decision, and accepted target record can be followed using exact IDs and versions, with one authoritative home per controlled record.
packages.interim: Existing document agreements and selected bought-tool record/review functions can provide these capabilities. Internal D1 storage is an option.
packages.later: Broader record schemas, managed policy/role configuration, and API exchange.
packages.basis: Shared capabilities must be available at their minimum level; they do not all require new internal software.
packages.effort: Main drivers: ownership decisions, usable existing data, destination formats, and internal-versus-external storage choice.

packages.title: Turn one source into reviewed needs and requirements
packages.outcome: A person captures a transcript, resolves questions, obtains cited candidate needs/requirements, reviews them and their links, and saves accepted outputs to the chosen home.
packages.gate: Complete the flow on a representative source; an independent check finds a deliberately unsupported statement; revisions receive fresh checks; accepted target IDs, citations, decisions, and correction reasons are retrievable.
packages.interim: Manual risk/task context, existing or bought-tool evidence/review, and current test/validation/release processes cover the rest of the lifecycle.
packages.later: CAP-07 document formats are optional; live Slack/meeting capture can be added independently through P-IN.
packages.basis: Drafting, checking, independent scrutiny, human acceptance, usable links, persistence/exchange, and feedback are required together for this promised outcome. AI extraction by itself is a smaller assistance feature.
packages.effort: Main drivers: fresh application/storage setup, prompt quality, citation reliability, reviewer workflow, and target-home exchange.

packages.title: Inspect traces and coordinate a significant change
packages.outcome: A reviewer sees known traces, assesses change consequences, independently inspects wider evidence, and assigns update/relink/retest work.
packages.gate: The threshold-change scenario exposes affected requirements, controls, tests, and labels; each finding has a version, reason, owner, and disposition. Missing context is visible.
packages.interim: An imported external relationship set and manual review can supply initial coverage. Existing owners/tools continue to implement and execute follow-up work.
packages.later: CAP-19 unlinked suggestions and CAP-20 drift automation are separate increments. Initial review can be manually triggered.
packages.basis: This package can precede P1 if existing records and links supply its inputs. P1 transcript ingestion is not a hard prerequisite.
packages.effort: Main drivers: existing graph quality, missing-link prevalence, impact-review breadth, evaluation cases, and integration with follow-up work.

packages.title: Connect implementation, verification, and normal developer work
packages.outcome: A team connects requirements/design to exact work/code/build references and reviewed test plans/executions at the relevant V-model levels.
packages.gate: A reviewer can follow a requirement to its design/build/test execution and disposition; failed and stale evidence remains distinguishable from current support.
packages.interim: Repository, CI, and work-tracker systems retain their facts. Manual references/imports and existing reviewers can start this workflow.
packages.later: CAP-25 adds checks in the PR/work path; CAP-39 supports unattended operations; selected P-IN adapters can arrive separately.
packages.basis: The minimum does not require every connector or a full automated release gate. CAP-25's developer-check workflow additionally needs change work and independent checking.
packages.effort: Main drivers: reference/mapping quality, report formats, execution identity, workflow permissions, and background-operation needs.

packages.title: Review baselines and produce selected outputs
packages.outcome: A team reviews an exact evidence state and produces a version-identifiable specification/report/package. Release support is a further scoped workflow.
packages.gate: The output identifies baseline, template, and evidence versions; a changed baseline/template produces a new output and an explainable difference.
packages.interim: Selected bought-tool baselines, documents, label records, and release processes can continue while internal output capabilities grow.
packages.later: CAP-30 label authoring and CAP-34 release/transfer support have additional evidence prerequisites. Full release takeover is a separate handover decision.
packages.basis: The baseline-to-document minimum does not depend on internal transcript intake or all automated developer integrations.
packages.effort: Main drivers: required outputs, template governance, target formats, evidence freshness, and scope of release support.

packages.title: Add selected source and engineering adapters
packages.outcome: Reduce manual capture for one selected source or engineering system using the common intake and identity contracts.
packages.gate: For each adapter, test capture, repeated capture, source revision/configuration mapping, failure visibility, and the relevant downstream review path.
packages.interim: Manual upload, paste, references, and report bundles remain usable between adapter deliveries.
packages.later: Choose Slack, meetings, tracker, repository, or CI independently according to actual friction and selected systems.
packages.basis: This is a grouping by shared integration work, not an all-or-nothing release package. There is no minimum bundle of all five adapters.
packages.effort: Main drivers: selected vendor APIs, permissions, field/report mappings, revision semantics, and unattended reliability.

packages.title: Extend risk records and control-evidence review
packages.outcome: Support the selected risk authoring/reference and control-evidence workflow.
packages.gate: A changed control identifies the related requirement/test evidence and risk decision to reconsider.
packages.interim: A bought tool or existing risk process can supply reviewed risk/control inputs from the first slice.
packages.later: Domain forms and broader effectiveness/risk-change assistance.
packages.basis: Risk information may be required early even when native risk authoring is delivered later.
packages.effort: Main drivers: product scope, existing risk data, analysis conventions, reviewers, and supporting evidence.

packages.title: Extend task, UI, and usability evidence
packages.gate: A critical task links to the relevant UI requirement, use-related risk, and evaluation outcome.
packages.interim: Existing design/study processes or a bought tool provide task and usability inputs meanwhile.
packages.later: Dedicated formative/summative work and coverage assistance.
packages.basis: This branch is selected by product scope and source availability, not by completion of all other domain modules.
packages.effort: Main drivers: study/task granularity, critical-task coverage, data formats, and design-system references.

packages.title: Extend validation and claim evidence
packages.outcome: Support per-need/per-claim evaluation plans, results, limitations, and decisions.
packages.gate: A reviewer can explain the evidence basis and limitations of a need/claim for the evaluated product configuration.
packages.interim: Existing validation/clinical processes or a bought tool continue to supply evidence and decisions.
packages.later: More study types and appropriate usability/model context.
packages.basis: Validation evidence is required where applicable; native validation workflow is an optional ownership choice.
packages.effort: Main drivers: applicable claims/needs, study types, evidence quality, and domain review responsibilities.

packages.title: Extend model and dataset evidence where applicable
packages.outcome: Connect exact model/data versions with implementation, performance, risk, and evaluation evidence.
packages.gate: A build/model/performance version mismatch is visible with the affected evidence references.
packages.interim: Selected model/dataset registries and current ML review practices retain artifact ownership.
packages.later: Registry adapters and domain-specific integrity/performance checks.
packages.basis: Conditional on product scope. A conventional software product need not build an ML module.
packages.effort: Main drivers: registry/data access, versioning, provenance, dataset partitions, and evaluation criteria.

packages.title: Learn from corrections from the first workflow
packages.outcome: Capture corrections, investigate recurring causes, and adopt evaluated changes to working methods.
packages.gate: A real correction has source/output/method references and a reason; a proposed method change is evaluated against failure and correct cases before adoption.
packages.interim: Manual feedback capture, a periodic human review, and an existing evaluation script/spreadsheet can supply the first meta-loop.
packages.later: Assisted cross-project pattern analysis and monitored method rollout.
packages.basis: Start CAP-35 with P1 or the first delivered workflow. Periodic analysis and evaluation can grow independently; a single important failure can trigger CAP-37 without waiting for CAP-36 pattern summaries.
packages.effort: Main drivers: feedback quality, reviewer effort, representative examples, evaluation coverage, and adoption ownership.

coverage.internal: Capture and citations for selected sources.
coverage.interim: Manual capture or existing/bought source intake covers unconnected formats/systems.
Product/domain owners still agree intended use, meaning, and claims; unsupported scope stays with the existing process.

coverage.internal: Drafting, inner checks, review, and trace links for the chosen requirement scope.
coverage.interim: Existing/bought requirements processes cover unimplemented types or deeper decomposition.

coverage.internal: Design/work/code references and independent significant-change checking.
coverage.interim: Current design, repository, PR, and work processes perform implementation and their own reviews.

coverage.internal: Selected risk/control records and change/coverage assistance.
coverage.interim: Risk owners and existing/bought risk management supply records, criteria, and decisions from day one.
Existing design/usability processes conduct studies and maintain unimplemented work.

coverage.internal: Versioned plans, execution associations, dispositions, and selected coverage checks.
coverage.interim: Developers/test owners and execution systems still run tests; other test workflows stay with existing/bought tools.

coverage.internal: Selected validation/claim records and review support.
coverage.interim: Validation/clinical/usability owners and their current or bought processes conduct and interpret evaluations.

coverage.internal: Recorded scope, linked/unlinked impact assistance, independent findings, and follow-up.
coverage.interim: Affected people decide consequences and complete updates/retests; existing change control covers unsupported scope.

coverage.internal: Exact evidence-state selection and coherence/review support.
coverage.interim: The chosen external review/baseline process remains authoritative until a scoped handover.

coverage.increment: P4 release increment after applicable prerequisites
coverage.internal: Current evidence association and separate readiness/release decisions.
coverage.interim: Existing/bought release/transfer process covers the complete job meanwhile, including evidence branches not yet internal.
